issues.detail: The Greek 'υπο του πνευματος' (by the Spirit) is rendered as 'được Thánh Linh đưa lên' (was led/taken up by the Holy Spirit). While 'by' can imply agency, the Vietnamese phrasing suggests a deliberate action of 'leading/taking' which is more specific than the Greek prepositional phrase used to describe the manner or agent of the movement.

The Greek 'πειρασθηναι' is an infinitive of purpose/result. The Vietnamese 'để chịu... cám dỗ' captures the purpose, but the phrase 'để chịu ma quỷ cám dỗ' omits the prepositional structure 'υπο του διαβολου' (by the devil) as a direct agent of the testing, instead making 'ma quỷ' (devil) an adjective-like modifier for 'cám dỗ' (temptation).
